name: AI Deep Dive — PLTR — 2026-05-02
rationale: Palantir is experiencing a massive growth inflection driven by its Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP). Trailing revenue grew 70% to $4.48B, and the company has achieved structural profitability with a 36.3% TTM net margin, yielding an exceptional 102.18 Rule of 40 score. However, this hypergrowth is entirely priced in at the current valuation (228.7x trailing P/E, 77.2x forward P/E). Even applying generous hypergrowth assumptions (34% CAGR) and a premium 50x exit multiple, our base case fair value sits at $122.92. The stock trades at a ~15% premium to this base case, making it slightly overvalued despite the phenomenal underlying business execution. SELL.

bear.rationale: Growth decelerates sharply to 25% as the initial AIP 'bootcamp' surge matures and commercial sales cycles lengthen. Net margin compresses to 30% due to increased sales and marketing expenses needed to acquire non-government customers. The exit P/E compresses to 40x. Stock-based compensation causes 2% annual dilution. The 1.1x quality multiplier reflects high switching costs within their government and defense contracts.
risks: Government spending contracts normalize post-geopolitical peaks
Commercial AIP adoption stalls as enterprises struggle to demonstrate ROI

base.rationale: Hypergrowth exception applied: initial analyst consensus of ~62% for Y1 smoothly decelerates to derive a 34% 5-year CAGR. Net margin remains exceptional at 36%, reflecting massive operating leverage on software scaling. The exit P/E remains elevated at 50x to account for Palantir's unique position as an AI platform for defense and critical enterprise. A quality multiplier of 1.2x is applied due to their near-monopoly in classified US government data ontology.
risks: Valuation premium vulnerable to any quarter where growth dips below 30%
Commercial sector competition from Microsoft (Fabric) and Databricks

bull.rationale: Catalyst: Palantir AIP becomes the definitive standard OS for corporate AI, penetrating the Global 2000 far faster than anticipated. Growth sustains a massive 42% CAGR over 5 years. Software operating leverage drives net margins up to an unprecedented 42%. The market awards a 65x exit P/E to reflect absolute dominance in the enterprise AI space. The 1.3x quality multiplier reflects a dual monopoly in Western defense intelligence and corporate AI orchestration.
risks: Extreme multiple (65x exit) assumes perfect execution and zero macro disruption

analyticsLog.marginAnchor: TTM 36.31% used. Palantir has structurally inflected from heavy losses (-19.6% two years ago) to massive profitability. Base case holds margin flat at 36% as a conservative estimate of steady-state SaaS operating leverage.
analyticsLog.growthDerivation: Hypergrowth exception applied. Analyst Y1 revenue implies 62.6% growth ($7.27B vs $4.47B TTM). Y2 implies 43.1%. Projecting a natural deceleration path (30%, 20%, 15% in years 3-5) yields a 5-yr CAGR of ~34%. Base case growth set to 34%.
analyticsLog.sectorBenchmarkRow: Technology — Software (SaaS): median P/E 30, best-in-class 50+. Used 50x for base case due to hypergrowth and AI premium.
dataQualityFlags: The massive divergence between trailing P/E (228x) and current margins indicates the market is entirely pricing the stock on future hypergrowth and its AI narrative.
analyticsLog.confidenceBreakdown: 0.85/1.0 — +0.10 for clean recent GAAP profitability and cash flow, -0.15 for the high sensitivity of the valuation to terminal growth and multiple assumptions.
